note: Running ffprobe for every segment inside the stream statistics request blocks all gunicorn threads once a few viewers open the details view, so the health check times out.

cause.title: feat: measure the real bitrate of each rendition
cause.author: Philipp Klinger
cause.patch:
diff --git a/video_app/api/streams.py b/video_app/api/streams.py
@@ -3,7 +3,24 @@ Statistics of an HLS stream, read from its playlist and segment files.
 """
 
 import math
 import os
+import subprocess
+
+# ffprobe per segment; the web image ships ffprobe for the upload check anyway.
+FFPROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30
+
+
+def _probe_bitrate(path):
+    """
+    Bit rate of one segment in bit/s as reported by ffprobe, or None if it cannot be read.
+    """
+    command = ["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=bit_rate", "-of", "csv=p=0", path]
+    try:
+        result = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=FFPROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, check=True)
+        return int(result.stdout.strip())
+    except (subprocess.SubprocessError, ValueError):
+        return None
 
 
 def _is_segment_name(name):

cause.body:
The bitrate in the details view was estimated from file sizes and the playlist
duration. ffprobe now reads the real bit rate of every segment, so the under
the hood view shows what the player actually receives.
